title: int hooks routes a hook-carrier defect to a whole-canon verb, and the remedy line does not say so
body:
`int hooks` diagnoses a hook-carrier problem and prints `intent claude upgrade --apply` as the remedy. That verb has no narrower mode: it applies the WHOLE canon set. So the only offered repair for one hook file also rewrites `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/settings.json`, and region-edits the pre-commit chain block -- and the remedy line says none of that.

## Measured

`intent claude upgrade` in report mode, on this tree, 2026-08-28:

```
canon (dry run): would apply v3 canon to /Users/matts/Devel/prj/Intent
  .claude/settings.json
  CLAUDE.md
  AGENTS.md
  usage-rules.md (only if absent)
  .intent_critic.yml (only if absent)
  .githooks/pre-commit.intent (the gate shim)
  .githooks/pre-commit (chain block, region-edited)
```

`intent claude upgrade --help` offers `--apply` and `--force` only. There is no flag that installs the carrier alone.

## The cost, which is not hypothetical

On 2026-08-28 an operator (intent-dc) met `int hooks` reporting this tree's dispatcher STALE -- a TRUE positive, the carrier was the 25609-byte install-time copy against a 34701-byte template. The operator dry-ran the printed remedy, saw that it also rewrote canon files owned by other workstreams in a tree that gates canon currency, and **declined to run it.** The stale carrier then stood for a further six hours until a coordinator applied the same verb deliberately, with the canon effects understood and stated in the commit.

**A correct diagnosis routed to a remedy wider than the defect does not get run.** The diagnosis was right, the remedy would have worked, and the gap between them cost the repair.

## What the fix is not

This is NOT a request to make the remedy narrower by default, and NOT a claim that applying canon is wrong -- `claude upgrade` applying the canon set is exactly what its name says. Two sufficient fixes, either alone:

- the remedy line states the full scope, so the operator can weigh it without dry-running the verb to find out; or
- a narrower path exists for the carrier alone, and the remedy names that instead.

## Falsifier

Run `int hooks` in an estate with a stale or absent carrier. If the printed remedy either names a carrier-only path, or states that the suggested verb also rewrites `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/settings.json` and the chain block, this is fixed.

## Scope note

Distinct from 0106 (the AT-grammar remedy string on a hook advisory), which is the WRONG remedy on the right subject. This one is the RIGHT remedy, undersold: it works, and its scope is not disclosed where it is offered.

Measured on this tree with the apply's real effects observed: the coordinator's run touched `AGENTS.md` (+12 blank lines from the renderer) beyond the two hook files; `settings.json` and `CLAUDE.md` were already canonical and `usage-rules.md` / `.intent_critic.yml` were preserved. **So the realised blast radius here was smaller than the declared one -- which is precisely why the declared scope, not the realised one, is what an operator needs at decision time.**
